final_answer:
Short answer: No, Client very likely cannot stop paying, and Lessor is very likely not responsible for the defective Trailers. Client's remedy lies against Manufacturer (now in Chapter 7), not Lessor. Caveat: I could not retrieve the statutory text from the official Virginia site (access blocked); the statutory propositions below rest on search-tool summaries of the Virginia Code and the uniform text, and no Virginia case law was located. Verify before reliance.

1. Governing law. A lease of goods (trailers) is governed by Virginia's UCC Article 2A, Va. Code Title 8.2A.

2. This is a 'finance lease' (Va. Code 8.2A-103(1)(g)). Three elements: (i) the lessor does not select, manufacture, or supply the goods; (ii) the lessor acquires the goods in connection with the lease; and (iii) one of several alternatives is met, including that the lessee receives a copy of the supply contract before signing the lease. Here Client itself picked the model and negotiated refrigeration specs with Manufacturer; Lessor merely bought the Trailers at Client's direction and financed them; and Lessor gave Client a full copy of the purchase agreement (including the warranty) before Client signed. All elements appear satisfied. The key fact is that Client, not Lessor, selected the goods. Lessor is a financier, not a seller. (Consumer lease exclusion does not apply: Client is a business.)

3. Hell-or-high-water. Va. Code 8.2A-407: for a finance lease that is not a consumer lease, the lessee's promises under the lease become irrevocable and independent upon the lessee's acceptance of the goods, and such a promise is enforceable between the parties and by or against third parties including assignees. This is self-executing, and the Lease's express 'absolute and unconditional, irrespective of any defense or setoff, counterclaim, or recoupment' language reinforces it. Client accepted and used the Trailers for four months before failures, so the promises became irrevocable on acceptance. Client's defense of Manufacturer's breakdown is therefore not a defense to rent owed Lessor, and withholding payment is a default under the Lease exposing Client to Lessor's remedies (Part 5, Art. C, 8.2A-523 et seq., e.g., accelerated rent/damages, repossession, per the Lease terms).

4. Lessor has no warranty liability. Implied warranties of merchantability (8.2A-212) do not apply 'except in a finance lease'; fitness warranty (8.2A-213) likewise is not imposed on a finance lessor who did not select the goods, and the Lease disclaims any Lessor warranties. Instead, 8.2A-209 gives Client the benefit of the supplier's promises and warranties under the supply contract (to the extent of its leasehold interest), subject to the supply contract's terms and defenses, without imposing duties on Lessor. Client keeps whatever direct rights it has against Manufacturer. The Lease's direction to take equipment claims to Manufacturer is consistent with the statute.

5. Revocation of acceptance is not a way out. Under 8.2A-517, the lessee generally may revoke acceptance for a substantial nonconformity, but the finance-lease carve-outs apply: revocation based on assumed cure is unavailable in a finance lease, and revocation based on lessor default is unavailable in a non-consumer finance lease. Acceptance made with knowledge of a nonconformity cannot be revoked in a finance lease. Also, the nonconformity here is a supplier problem, not a lessor default. (Note: the search summaries of 8.2A-517 suggest some revocation against the lessor may remain where the lessor's assurances induced acceptance; there is no such fact here, since Lessor made no assurances.)

6. Manufacturer's bankruptcy does not shift risk to Lessor. The finance-lease structure allocates supplier-insolvency risk to the lessee. The trustee's refusal to honor warranty claims leaves Client with at most an unsecured Chapter 7 claim (file a proof of claim) against Manufacturer's estate; it does not make the warranty claim Lessor's problem. Lessor also does not step into Manufacturer's warranty obligations.

7. Possible exceptions / counterarguments (none apparent on the facts): (a) unconscionability, 8.2A-108, requires unconscionability at the time of contracting; a negotiated commercial lease with a standard hell-or-high-water clause by a business lessee is unlikely to qualify; (b) if Lessor had selected, supplied, or made representations about the Trailers, or Client had not received the supply contract (not the case), finance-lease status could fail; (c) Lessor's own fraud, misrepresentation, or bad-faith conduct is not alleged; (d) Client's notice duty under 8.2A-516 (notify lessor and supplier of default within a reasonable time or be barred as to the unnotified party) is relevant to preserving claims; (e) the Lease terms (cure, default, remedies, insurance, Lessor's mitigation duties) should be read, and a lessor must still act in good faith and in a commercially reasonable manner in enforcement.

Practical: Client should keep paying under reservation of rights, give written notice of the defects to Lessor, preserve its warranty claim by filing a proof of claim in Manufacturer's Chapter 7 case, check for any third-party (compressor maker) warranty or service contract that may extend to Client under 8.2A-209, consider repair at its own cost, and negotiate with Lessor (workout or substitution) if nonpayment is unavoidable. Stopping payment risks default, acceleration, repossession and deficiency liability.

authorities.title: Definitions - finance lease
authorities.proposition: Finance lease: lessor does not select, manufacture or supply goods; acquires goods in connection with lease; and lessee receives copy of supply contract before signing (among alternatives).

authorities.title: Irrevocable promises: finance leases
authorities.proposition: In a non-consumer finance lease, lessee's promises become irrevocable and independent upon acceptance; enforceable between parties and by or against assignees.

authorities.title: Lessee under finance lease as beneficiary of supply contract
authorities.proposition: Benefit of supplier's promises and warranties extends to finance lessee, subject to supply contract terms and defenses; imposes no duty on lessor and does not modify supply contract rights.

authorities.title: Implied warranty of merchantability
authorities.proposition: Implied merchantability warranty applies except in a finance lease.

authorities.title: Revocation of acceptance of goods
authorities.proposition: Finance-lease limits on revocation of acceptance: not on assumption of cure; not for lessor default in non-consumer finance lease; no revocation for nonconformity known at acceptance.

authorities.title: Effect of acceptance; notice of default
authorities.proposition: Lessee must notify lessor and supplier within a reasonable time of discovered default or be barred from remedy against party not notified.

authorities.title: Unconscionability
authorities.proposition: Court may refuse to enforce or limit a clause found unconscionable at the time made.

claims.text: The Lease is a non-consumer finance lease because Client selected the Trailers and negotiated specs with Manufacturer, Lessor merely acquired and financed them, and Client received the supply contract before signing.
Upon acceptance, Client's payment promises became irrevocable and independent; Manufacturer's defects and bankruptcy are not a defense or setoff, so Client cannot lawfully stop paying Lessor.

Lessor is not responsible for the defective Trailers: no implied warranties in a finance lease, no express Lessor warranty, and Client's recourse is to Manufacturer under the supply-contract warranty extended by 8.2A-209.
Revocation of acceptance against Lessor is substantially foreclosed in a non-consumer finance lease absent Lessor default or inducing assurances.
Unconscionability and notice are the principal residual issues; neither appears to change the outcome on these facts.
